notes.detailedSummary: Van der Put explicitly assumes an algebraically closed field. An elementary root-approximation argument verifies algebraic closure after completion, including positive characteristic. Berkovich’s rigid-domain comparison is distinguished from an ordinary-neighborhood assertion. Canonical predecessor notes and the controlling INCONCLUSIVE review are preserved without importing their mathematical claims.
notes.text:
Van der Put, Ann. Inst. Fourier 30(4) (1980), 155–164, introduction p.155, assumes a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. Theorem 1.1 states that every one-dimensional normal connected affinoid space is an affinoid subspace of a nonsingular complete curve. Its strict-affinoid convention and complete proof ending were checked. It does not grant arbitrary-K finite-separable algebraization.

The needed field fact has an elementary proof. For a monic degree-d polynomial F over the completion of an algebraically closed valued field A, choose B≥1 bounding its coefficients, ε_m decreasing to zero, and monic F_m over A with coefficient error at most ε_m^d B^{−(d−1)}. All roots of F_m have norm at most B by leading-term dominance. Given a root r_m, |F_{m+1}(r_m)|≤ε_m^d. Factoring F_{m+1} shows that some root r_{m+1} lies within ε_m of r_m. Ultrametricity makes these roots Cauchy, and their limit is a root of F. Induction factors every polynomial, including inseparable ones. Integral monic lifts and reduction of their factorizations prove residue algebraic closure. Taking roots gives a divisible value group; nontriviality makes its logarithm contain a dense nonzero rational line. These facts justify the field scope C=completion(algebraic closure K), but prove no current transport.

Berkovich, Publ. Math. IHÉS 78 (1993), Theorem 1.6.1 and Lemma 1.6.2(i), DOI 10.1007/BF02712916, concern Hausdorff strict spaces over a nontrivially valued field. They identify rigid affinoid domains with Berkovich affinoid domains; ordinary-interior identification remains a separate analytic application.

The supplied causal-evidence hash dfc96b12afe112f6eccb35d34417a4199892ded5501305edae0aa15f55c912d3 was matched. Cached official evidence identifies Thuillier tel-00010990v1; this run made no live retrieval. Exactly three, five and two canonical notes were selected from the round-16, round-17 and round-21 run.json results. The controlling round-16 review remains INCONCLUSIVE with 23 premises and 19 passages. No predecessor theorem or verdict was accepted as a premise. The requested round-17 proof-core.md is absent; the actual repair-core.md was inspected. Different CLD text extractions have identical underlying v2 PDF bytes, so their LF coordinates must name their particular cache.

notes.summary: Proved a fixed-cycle rational-slope obstruction and elementary tree, cap and monotone-shift calculations. Exact finite diagnostics pass; no analytic counterexample or approximation theorem follows.
notes.detailedSummary: Parallel edges of lengths 1 and sqrt(2) obstruct rational affine approximation on those same unsubdivided edges, with uniform error at least 1/2. Refinements remain outside the negative claim. A subtree construction proves positive interior Laplacian and rational strictification on a given metric tree. Convex caps and tail shifts are proved conditionally on already existing analytic neighborhoods and approximants. Exact checks cover 1,441 trees and 85,787 boundary assignments.
notes.text:
A discarded approach is independent rational rounding on an arbitrary fixed skeletal graph. Take vertices v0,v1, boundary vertices b0,b1, two parallel v0–v1 edges of lengths 1 and √2, and length-1 edges vi–bi. Set F(v0)=0, F(v1)=1, F(b0)=−1−1/√2 and F(b1)=2+1/√2, extending affinely. The outgoing slopes sum to zero at both interior vertices, so F is metric-graph harmonic.

If a continuous G has rational affine slopes q1,q2 on these SAME UNSUBDIVIDED parallel edges, continuity forces G(v1)−G(v0)=q1=q2√2. Irrationality of √2 forces both slopes zero. Indeed, a reduced fraction a/b satisfying a²=2b² would make both a and b even. Thus G(v0)=G(v1), and 1≤|F(v1)−G(v1)|+|G(v0)−F(v0)|≤2||G−F||∞. Such functions cannot approximate F within error less than 1/2. This does not obstruct subdivisions or other constructions and is not an analytic counterexample to P06.2.

On a finite metric TREE with nonempty boundary B, choose root b∈B. Set μ=1 at interior vertices I, μ(b)=−|I| and zero at other boundary vertices. Give each child-to-parent edge slope equal to the sum of μ over the child subtree, and integrate from root value zero. Path uniqueness defines a continuous integer-slope function ψ. Its outgoing sum at each vertex equals μ: subtract the child-subtree sums from its own subtree sum; at the root use Σμ=0. Therefore Δψ=1 on I. If ΔF≥0 there, F+δψ has margin δ. Rational slopes within η integrate consistently on the tree, with uniform error at most Lη and Laplacian error at most deg(v)η. Choosing η<δ/(2 max interior degree) preserves positivity. This proves a graph calculation, not actual analytic chart realization.

For an even smooth probability kernel supported in (−1,1), let χ_η=|·|*ρ_η and m_η(s,t)=(s+t+χ_η(s−t))/2. Convexity, |χ_η′|≤1 and zero first moment show that m_η is smooth convex, nondecreasing in both variables, equals max when |s−t|≥η, and lies between max and max+η/2. For a,r>0 and η<ar, m_η(c−at,c−ar) equals the old affine function through t≤r−η/a and the NEW constant c−ar from t≥r+η/a. Its error relative to c is at most ar+η/2. Actual whole annular collars and exact ordinary overlaps are additional obligations.

If approximants already constructed on ONE compact Y satisfy ||g_n−f||∞≤b_n=4^(−n), set c_n=Σ_{j≥n}(b_j+b_{j+1})=(5/3)b_n. Then u_n=g_n+c_n decreases because c_n−c_{n+1}=b_n+b_{n+1}; moreover 0≤u_n−f≤(8/3)b_n. Constants preserve smoothness and psh already possessed by g_n. This supplies neither the approximants nor a common domain.

diagnostics/finite_checks.py uses exact fractions and Prüfer enumeration. diagnostics/output.json reports 1,441 labelled trees of orders 2–6 and all 85,787 nonempty-boundary assignments, with zero Laplacian failures. Edge k in decoder order has length (k+2)/(k+1); case counts are n^(n−2)(2^n−1), namely [3,21,240,3875,81648]. Among 2,209 pairs from 47 rationals a/b with −6≤a≤6 and 1≤b≤6, only zero slopes satisfy the parallel-edge continuity equation in Q(√2). One hundred exact tail identities also pass. These are exhaustive finite results only for the stated domains; the universal claims have the written proofs above. Rerun python diagnostics/finite_checks.py > diagnostics/output.json or bash reproduce.sh. The complete diagnostic arguments are in P06.2-argument.md.
